visual_action: A video montage. The first clip shows a close-up of Donald Trump speaking at a podium with American flags in the background, with '2024' overlaid. This is followed by a series of clips with '2026' overlaid, showing Trump speaking at different podiums (once while wearing a 'USA' hat) and another man, Pete Hegseth, speaking at a podium.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: Appears speaking in multiple clips and is the subject of the video's central claim, which contrasts his past and present statements on war.

cast.name: Pete Hegseth
cast.evidence: Appears in one clip speaking about war casualties, identified by face-ID.

spoken_summary: The video juxtaposes a 2024 clip of Donald Trump promising to stop wars with a montage of 2026 clips. In the 2024 clip, Trump says, "I'm not going to start a war. I'm going to stop wars." In the 2026 clips, both Trump and Pete Hegseth speak about a military effort involving American casualties. Trump states, "we may have casualties that often happens in war," and, "There will likely be more."
audio_music: A somber, dramatic orchestral track plays throughout the video, creating a serious and foreboding tone that underscores the discussion of war and casualties.
editing_pacing: A montage with quick cuts that juxtaposes clips from two different years, 2024 and 2026, to create a direct and stark contrast. Text overlays are used to label the years.
central_claim: Donald Trump is a liar who broke his 2024 promise to avoid wars and is now, in 2026, overseeing a war with American casualties.
intended_effect: To persuade the viewer that Donald Trump is untrustworthy and has failed to keep his promises regarding foreign policy, thereby generating opposition to him.
